bio: Sanjiv Jaiswal ‘Sanjay’ is a senior official in the Ministry of Railways. He has published over 600 stories, 5 novels and 7 collections for children. His books have won awards at the national level.

Ajit Narayan is a professional cartoonist who has been drawing for 
reputed publishing houses for over 14 years.  As a cartoonist consultant 
for Scholastic India, he has been conducting cartoon workshops in 
schools, within and outside Delhi since the year 2000. He is the author 
of the book Cartooning with Ajit Narayan.
Manisha Chaudhry is an author, editor and translator.  When she needs to rejuvenate, she rushes off to the mountains to trek and to catch up with Urdu poetry.
Parismita wrote this story for a ‘Pratham’ program in Delhi. She is currently working on comic books.
Utkarsha Manish has written content for an educational website. She has also been writing articles on Nature and its conservation for magazines and newspapers.

Cheryl Rao writes stories and articles for children and adults and has been published by Orient Blackswan, Harper Collins, Children’s Book Trust and others. She has also jointly written a resource book on creative writing, Anyone Can Write. She dedicates this book to Timir and Sheba.
Mala Kumar is a freelance journalist, and an editor with Pratham Books. If possible, she would spend all her time trading stories with children.

Tanvi Bhat is a freelance illustrator who lives in Mumbai and loves the rains. She's a self-taught artist who loves to draw for children's books. She works with water colours and gouache and gets her inspiration from things she sees when out exploring the streets of colourful India.
Yamini is an editor at Pratham Books. In her free time, she likes to escape to green spaces and take photographs.

Umesh has been working with children for 14 years in the fields of theatre and education. He is very interested in theatre as a teaching method and as an approach to understand the self. His other interests include music, cinema and writing plays.

Rajiv Eipe lives in Bangalore and works on Animation and Illustration projects. He also likes to doodle in his sketchbook, drink more coffee than is good for him, maintain an untidy workspace and gaze into vacant space at short intervals.
Myself, a Waldorf homeschooler, a theatre artist, a tree climber..I love to cycle and hike. as my hair greys, i remain a child at heart
Vinayak Varma is a writer and visual artist based in Bangalore, India. He is the author and illustrator of 'Jadav and the Tree-Place' and 'Angry Akku'.
